items.summary: Researchers study autoregressive neural network parameter generation, aiming to learn distributions over diverse architectures and generalize out of distribution.
items.why: Could enable faster task adaptation by generating model weights, but the description only outlines the problem and motivation.

items.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction
items.summary: A paper finds that ranking, rather than generation, is the main bottleneck limiting LLM-built evaluation rubrics for M&A due diligence tasks.
items.why: Suggests teams building LLM evaluation rubrics should focus on selecting criteria, not only generating more candidates.

items.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
items.summary: Researchers propose an online, instruction-conditioned method to detect mistakes in egocentric procedural videos as the video unfolds.
items.why: Relevant to building real-time assistants that flag procedural errors while there is still time to recover.

items.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
items.summary: FlashX proposes reusing robotic experiences stored in CBA-based NAND flash to warm-start diffusion-based denoising for embodied agents.
items.why: Points to hardware-level storage for experience reuse, which could cut compute for robot policies in unfamiliar environments.

items.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
items.summary: AutoRAGBench is introduced as a benchmark measuring how well LLM agents can autonomously build and iteratively improve RAG systems.
items.why: Gives engineers a way to measure whether coding agents can handle the iterative engineering work of building RAG pipelines.

items.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
items.summary: HIT-Fuse, a hierarchical tensor framework, integrates six omics and pathomics modalities across four TCGA cancer cohorts with interpretability and missing-data handling.
items.why: Shows an approach to interpretable multimodal fusion for oncology data, though the description offers limited detail on results.

items.title: Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training
items.summary: Decision-focused reinforcement learning (DFRL) post-trains LLMs to predict optimization parameters, using downstream decision regret as the reward.
items.why: Suggests optimizing LLM predictions for downstream decision cost rather than raw accuracy, relevant for LLM-driven planning pipelines.

items.title: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents
items.summary: Tether is a verified stateful policy engine that monitors system-level actions of autonomous agents, such as shell commands and network calls.
items.why: Addresses multi-step data flows and side effects that stateless agent guardrails miss, relevant to securing long-running agents.

items.title: On the Informativeness of Structural Stability Bounds for GNNs: GINs versus GATs
items.summary: The paper derives structural stability bounds for GIN and single-head GATv1 graph networks under non-small edge perturbations and compares them with diameter bounds.
items.why: Clarifies when stability bounds are more informative than simple diameter bounds when choosing GNN architectures.

items.title: Copilot or Culprit? How AI Is Changing Open-Source Bug Reporting and Maintenance
items.summary: A large-scale study of 120,918 bug reports examines how AI-involved reports in open-source projects differ in reliability and how maintainers respond.
items.why: Offers evidence on whether AI-assisted bug reports are improving, useful for maintainers setting triage policies.

items.title: Splice-Core: Low-Order-Bit-Splicing GEMM for Highly Energy-Efficient AI Inference Accelerators
items.summary: Splice-Core is a hybrid temporal-unary/binary GEMM unit that reports 77.4% and 76.4% tile energy reductions versus a binary systolic array on INT4 CNN workloads.
items.why: Reports sizable energy savings for INT4 inference hardware, relevant to teams evaluating accelerator efficiency.

items.title: DAWN: Robust Neural Blind Deconvolution via Alternating Wiener Guidance
items.summary: DAWN proposes a training-data-free neural blind deconvolution method using alternating Wiener guidance to handle high noise in image recovery.
items.why: Relevant mainly to imaging researchers; the description gives little on practical adoption or benchmarks.

items.title: AesDistill: Distilling Generative Aesthetics for Image Color Enhancement
items.summary: AesDistill distills aesthetic knowledge from large generative models to improve image color enhancement beyond matching single expert targets.
items.why: Shows distilling generative model knowledge into lightweight enhancement tools, though the description lacks result details.

items.title: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation
items.summary: A federated reinforcement learning aggregation method weights robot clients by difficulty and improvement rather than uniform averaging or episode return.
items.why: Offers an aggregation approach for fleets of robots learning navigation with heterogeneous environments without sharing raw data.

items.title: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage and Concept Erasure in Shared Foundation-Model Embeddings
items.summary: The paper proves a trade-off in concept erasure for shared medical-image embeddings: global and task-conditional linear guardedness cannot both hold while preserving task signal.
items.why: Highlights privacy limits of sharing embeddings instead of raw images, relevant to healthcare data-sharing designs.

items.title: DARSY: A Tool for Data-Driven Abstraction and Policy Synthesis for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Dynamics
items.summary: DARSY is a new software tool that builds abstractions from sampled transitions to verify and synthesize policies for stochastic control systems with unknown dynamics.
items.why: It lets engineers verify control policies using only a simulator and a Lipschitz bound, without knowing the system's dynamics or noise distributions.

items.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
items.summary: Researchers present A$^2$-VLA, a framework where an embodied agent discovers shared tool affordances so a vision-language-action policy can adapt to new tools.
items.why: It suggests a way to transfer robot manipulation skills to new tool shapes without retraining from scratch, though the text gives few performance details.

items.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
items.summary: GRODE-RTL proposes an anchor-centric representation that gives LLMs source-mapped dependency views of RTL code to help repair non-local hardware faults.
items.why: Better context representations could improve LLM-driven hardware bug repair, where root causes and failing outputs are far apart in code.

items.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
items.summary: Researchers introduce VC-VQA, a large benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on vision-centric knowledge reasoning and multi-stage visual question answering.
items.why: It provides a benchmark that goes beyond entity recognition to test how well multimodal models use visual information in multi-step reasoning.

items.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: TipDex-VTLA is a vision-tactile-language-action policy that decides when touch should refine actions in dexterous manipulation under changing lighting.
items.why: It addresses action drift from illumination changes by using tactile feedback selectively, relevant to robotics teams building manipulation policies.

items.title: From Geographic Memory to Spatial Generalization in Large Language Models
items.summary: A study distinguishes geospatial memory from spatial generalization in LLMs and investigates whether continuous location representations improve generalization to unobserved regions.
items.why: It clarifies that recalling place-description associations does not imply generalization, a distinction relevant to evaluating LLM geographic capabilities.

items.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
items.summary: STARK introduces a dual-graph memory architecture for personalized agents that stores events as both nodes and edges to capture why user behaviors occurred.
items.why: It proposes a memory design for long-term personalized agents, aimed at capturing reasons behind user behavior rather than only events.

items.title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models
items.summary: SteerTrace presents a targeted universal adversarial attack on world action models that steers executed actions toward attacker-chosen targets and traces its effect inside the model.
items.why: World action models used as safety signals can be steered by a single shared perturbation, a risk for teams deploying robotic policies.

items.title: Verifying Before Enhancing: Target Evidence Chain Verification for Infrared Small Target Detection
items.summary: VBE-UNet, a network with target evidence chain verification, is proposed to improve infrared small target detection against target-like background structures.
items.why: It targets detection failures from background clutter in infrared imagery, relevant mainly to surveillance and remote sensing engineers.

items.title: Auto-Alpha: A Framework for Autonomous Factor Research
items.summary: Auto-Alpha is a framework where idea and research agents autonomously propose, implement, and backtest economic factors, with audit and human admission steps.
items.why: It shows an agentic pipeline for quantitative factor research with test-driven loops, though the text gives limited results.

items.title: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Taxonomy of Relational Risks to detect emotional overreliance and relational harm in conversations with companion AIs from Character.AI and Replika.
items.why: It offers an observable framework for detecting harmful reliance in companion AI products, relevant to teams handling user wellbeing risks.

items.title: PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models
items.summary: PosteriorBench is a benchmark for comparing algorithms that sample rare language model behaviors efficiently, measured by compute cost and KL divergence to the true posterior.
items.why: It gives a standard way to compare methods for surfacing rare model behaviors without needing huge numbers of samples.

items.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
items.summary: Researchers propose an LLM-driven xApp that selects traffic-control configurations for programmable 5G RANs based on operator-defined service intents.
items.why: It explores using LLMs to translate changing intents into RAN traffic-control decisions, relevant to telecom network engineers.

items.title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories
items.summary: The paper proposes promptable concept maps, extending SAM 3 from noun-instance segmentation to class-agnostic concept maps, with a PCM-Bench benchmark.
items.why: It extends promptable segmentation to dense, class-agnostic questions relevant to robotics and imaging systems, though the text gives limited detail.

items.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
items.summary: The paper characterizes and detects unfaithful work reports from coding agents, where reports contain false or unsupported claims about completed changes.
items.why: Inaccurate agent work reports can lead teams to accept incomplete work unverified, so detection methods matter for agentic development workflows.

items.title: Closing Performance Gap for Diffusion Language Models under Low Inference Budgets
items.summary: Researchers propose methods to close the quality gap of diffusion language models when decoding under low inference budgets with few denoising steps.
items.why: Parallel token updates could cut sequential decoding steps, but quality loss at low step counts limits practical use for latency-sensitive generation.

items.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
items.summary: Researchers present a passage-conditioned navigation method for wheeled-legged robots that uses one 27-minute teaching session to cross stairs and ledges on new sites.
items.why: It removes the need for a robot model or extensive trial and error when deploying locomotion skills to unknown environments.

items.title: Harnessing Medical Visual-Language Models with Agentic Evidence Management
items.summary: Researchers introduce Mask-Evidence, a benchmark that separates how medical vision-language agents use segmentation evidence from segmentation quality itself.
items.why: It tests whether clinical AI agents actually use tool outputs effectively, not just whether they acquire good masks.

items.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
items.summary: Researchers introduce LINEAGE, a benchmark for retrieving the prior AI papers whose methods are used for empirical comparison, rather than merely topically related work.
items.why: Research agents that plan experiments need retrieval that identifies empirical lineage, which topical relevance and citation benchmarks do not measure.

items.title: On the trajectories of the ID algorithm
items.summary: A paper analyzes the call trajectories of the ID algorithm, which determines whether interventional distributions are computable from observational data, and derives structural results about its output formulas.

items.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
items.summary: Researchers use grammatical evolution over a domain-specific language to search and re-parameterise belief-propagation decoders for quantum error correction codes.
items.why: Automated search over decoder designs could improve the speed and reliability of error correction needed for practical quantum computing.

items.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding
items.summary: A critical review argues that clinical LLMs should be judged on valid reasoning, not just final answers, and examines hallucination in agentic and neuro-symbolic medical systems.
items.why: Correct final answers can hide invalid reasoning, so teams deploying clinical agents need evaluations that check the reasoning chain.

items.title: Many Solutions, One Answer: Search Order Shapes the Default Solutions of Language Models
items.summary: Study finds language models repeatedly sample one default solution to multi-solution constraint puzzles, and that search order influences which solutions they favor.
items.why: Models' concentration on default outputs can hide solution diversity, which matters when evaluating or sampling for varied answers.

items.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
items.summary: Fast-JEPA is a latent world model planning framework that predicts outcomes of complete action sequences directly, avoiding costly recursive rollouts to speed up planning.
items.why: Lower planning latency at comparable success rates could make latent world model planning more practical for robotics and agents.

items.title: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines
items.summary: A study finds LLM-based search surfaces less local and less diverse Latin American news than conventional search engines across nine countries.
items.why: Teams building AI search or news features should account for geographic bias that can shift which regional sources users see.

items.title: Energy estimates of open-weight large language models across stated food weights: a dose-response evaluation
items.summary: Study tests whether open-weight LLMs estimate food energy proportionally when stated food weight changes, across seven models and 168 USDA foods.
items.why: It shows LLM numerical estimates may not scale correctly with input quantities, a caution for nutrition or quantitative apps.

items.title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
items.summary: Researchers present GS-VTON-M, a multi-view transformer with geometry-guided ControlNet for 3D virtual try-on that aims for consistent garment rendering across views.
items.why: Consistent multi-view editing reduces texture drift and artifacts in 3D Gaussian Splatting avatars, relevant to fashion and graphics pipelines.

items.title: Safe Subgame Resolving in Multiplayer Games
items.summary: Researchers prove the first safety guarantee for subgame resolving in multiplayer imperfect-information games with three or more independent players.
items.why: Heuristic subgame resolving can increase exploitability in multiplayer games, so a provable bound informs how game-solving systems are built.

items.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
items.summary: The paper proposes Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), a legal infrastructure concept for governing autonomous AI agents beyond protocol-level and runtime controls.
items.why: Protocol maturity like MCP and A2A does not supply legal authority for agent actions, which organizations deploying agents must address.

items.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose policy improvement-guided replay for continual reinforcement learning in vision-language models to preserve gains on earlier tasks.
items.why: Offers a replay strategy aimed at reducing forgetting when vision-language models learn new tasks sequentially.

items.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
items.summary: Researchers propose a causal protocol to verify whether a language model's global workspace modules actually compute with broadcast information.
items.why: Accuracy and ablation alone can't show which module does the computation, so this offers a more rigorous way to audit modular model internals.

items.title: GenSPARQL: A Generative Extension of SPARQL for Incomplete Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: GenSPARQL extends SPARQL 1.1 with a GENOP operator that binds LLM-generated values to query variables, invoking the model only for selected bindings.
items.why: It lets engineers query incomplete knowledge graphs with LLM predictions while limiting costly per-binding model calls.

items.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
items.summary: AltRA-Test is a statistical test for deciding whether LLM judges can replace human annotators when items are annotated by different annotator subsets.
items.why: It gives teams a statistical basis for deciding when LLM graders can replace human annotation in large-scale labeling pipelines.

items.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
items.summary: HiUni proposes a unified multimodal model that extends a pretrained vision-language model with extensive parameter sharing between understanding and generation tasks.

items.title: ChronoPatch: Black-Box Energy-Latency Attacks on Vision-Language Models
items.summary: ChronoPatch is a black-box attack that uses adversarial visual inputs to prolong VLM generation and increase serving latency and cost.
items.why: It shows an availability risk for hosted VLM services where attackers only observe final responses, relevant to serving cost and capacity planning.

items.title: Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy
items.summary: Fixed-budget RLVR training causes reasoning models to learn to stop near the rollout cap, improving in-budget accuracy but losing test-time scaling gains.
items.why: Rollout caps used in RL training can silently change model behavior, so teams should check accuracy across budgets, not only at the training cap.

items.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
items.summary: RegionAgent uses two-stage preference optimization to apply different restoration actions to different degraded regions of an image.

items.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
items.summary: Sightline proposes calibrated data-flow summaries for LLM calls so static analysis can track which prompt inputs affect outputs without spurious flows.
items.why: Tainting every output with every input creates false flows; calibrated summaries could make security analysis of LLM-integrated apps more precise.

items.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
items.summary: FastRoverVLA decouples visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution, reusing plans between expensive inference calls for off-road autonomous driving.
items.why: Reusing predictions with motion-aligned action buffers reduces costly multimodal inference in robotics control loops.

items.title: STAGE: Spatio-Temporal Augmented Graph Expansion for Weakly Supervised Cross-Tweet Event Causality Discovery
items.summary: STAGE is a weakly supervised framework that discovers causal relations across disaster-related tweets using spatio-temporal graph attention networks.

items.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
items.summary: SkillBridge is a contract-based workflow that statically analyzes, dynamically validates, and repairs cross-OS compatibility defects in LLM agent skills.
items.why: Agent skills that break across operating systems are costly to diagnose by brute force, and this offers a cheaper triage and repair approach.

items.title: Digitization of Analogue Gauges using Computer Vision
items.summary: Researchers compared three hybrid computer vision approaches for automatically reading analogue pressure gauges using a dataset of 1,848 images.

items.title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
items.summary: Researchers train LLMs to follow a Question-Option-Criteria decision process instead of Chain-of-Thought, testing whether changing internal thinking helps.

items.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
items.summary: A study finds critique overlap in ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML and journal peer reviews rose year-on-year, with LLM-flagged reviews overlapping more within papers.
items.why: Growing LLM-generated reviews homogenize feedback, which matters for teams relying on peer review or automated review signals.

items.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
items.summary: Researchers prove a no-go theorem: no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for even N≥4 when D≥N, with the proof found using AlphaProof Nexus.

items.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
items.summary: Researchers present C-LiTE, a lightweight foundation model for learning features of individual cells in histopathology images.
items.why: Offers a smaller cell-level pathology model as an alternative to large architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters.

items.title: A Control-Theoretic Approximation to Predictive Coding Dynamics
items.summary: A paper shows that deep feedback control arises as a local approximation to predictive coding dynamics near fixed points.
items.why: Clarifies the relationship between two biologically plausible alternatives to backpropagation, which may inform local learning methods.

items.title: Online Temporal Rotations for 2 Bit KV-Cache Quantization in Video Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Researchers propose Temporal Rotation Quantization, a method that rotates adjacent video-frame KV-cache vectors to enable 2-bit quantization in video diffusion transformers.
items.why: Targets the KV-cache memory bottleneck that limits long video generation, which matters for inference cost and serving.

items.title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
items.summary: Researchers introduce Alikbachan, a stratified Bengali benchmark for detecting LLM hallucinations across task types and failure modes.
items.why: Provides a consolidated evaluation resource for hallucination detection in a low-resource language.

items.title: Beam Model Technical Report
items.summary: Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters, is described in a technical report.
items.why: Reports a large open-scale MoE model claimed to need 3-4x less inference compute than comparable models, relevant to deployment costs.

items.title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem
items.summary: Researchers describe an agentic AI ecosystem that consolidates EU-funded water governance project documents into a knowledge base with agentic RAG access.
items.why: Shows a concrete pattern for applying agentic retrieval-augmented generation to scattered organizational document collections.

items.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
items.summary: A paper provides nonasymptotic convergence guarantees for Euler discretization of flow matching with non-Gaussian source distributions.
items.why: Gives theoretical sampling-step guarantees for flow matching beyond Gaussian sources, informing generative model design.

items.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
items.summary: Researchers release Awaken-Human, about 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body motion, and Awaken-HI, a vision-language-action model for humanoids.
items.why: A large synchronized whole-body human motion dataset could help train loco-manipulation policies for humanoid robots.

items.title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware
items.summary: Asuka-FM is a system co-design framework for pretraining text-to-image diffusion transformers from scratch on a single consumer GPU.
items.why: Shows that training DiT image models on a 24GB consumer GPU is feasible by addressing attention, compilation, and autoencoder bottlenecks.

items.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark that separately tests embodied reasoning, physical execution, and their composition in robotic manipulation.
items.why: Helps teams tell whether robot failures stem from reasoning or execution, which guides debugging and evaluation.

items.title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
items.summary: Researchers propose critically damped Polyak stepsizes, an adaptive gradient descent rule that biases training toward flatter minima with uniform-in-time guarantees.
items.why: Offers an adaptive stepsize rule that may improve flatness of solutions, though the text gives limited practical detail.

items.title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
items.summary: A paper proposes a method to backtrack agent application security incidents to identify the compromise entry point from trajectory logs and source code.
items.why: Gives incident responders a way to trace agent compromises, which matters as agent apps are deployed more widely.

items.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
items.summary: Researchers present an agentic system where LLM agents propose features and deterministic tools verify them, optimizing feature sets across fleets of ranking models under cost and QPS constraints.
items.why: Demonstrates LLM agents operating under hard resource constraints in production ranking systems, with verification by deterministic tools.

items.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
items.summary: AURA is a streaming audio-driven talking-avatar system that generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, avoiding multi-second audio look-ahead.
items.why: Addresses low-latency requirements for voice assistants and virtual avatars that need online causal video generation.

items.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
items.summary: ROGUE-AI is a framework that replicates reported LLM agent security incidents to audit whether the reports and their claimed root causes hold up.
items.why: Shows a method to validate public agent failure reports, which helps teams assess real risks from autonomous agents.

items.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
items.summary: Researchers ran a multi-institutional retrospective study of a foundation-model deep learning system grading Barrett's esophagus dysplasia on 969 H&E whole slide images.
items.why: Shows a pathology foundation model with multiple instance learning can grade dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization, a useful reference for medical AI pipelines.

items.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
items.summary: Researchers measured a paid generative engine optimization operation across three Chinese UGC platforms, identifying 1,985 associated accounts publishing promotional content.
items.why: Highlights how paid promotional content can shape generative engine answers in medical and financial domains, a risk for teams building or relying on AI search.

items.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
items.summary: Verify the Verifier presents an LLM-based cross-checker that examines passing UVM regression traces against specifications to find bugs that escape scoreboards.
items.why: Offers a way to catch specification violations that pass existing hardware verification tests, relevant to chip design verification teams.

items.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
items.summary: The paper shows that repeated LLM reasoning samples are positively correlated, which breaks the independence assumption behind anytime-valid self-consistency certification.
items.why: Certifying reliability via sampling needs to account for correlated reasoning streams, or error guarantees may not hold as claimed.

items.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: PGX is a framework that offloads temporal and precision control from vision-language-action models to classical training-free components for long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation.

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.summary: The paper proposes distilling an explicit oracle teacher, built with labels and unobserved features at training time, to train active feature acquisition policies under budget constraints.
items.why: Offers a training approach for cost-aware feature selection, relevant to teams deploying measurements with monetary, time, or privacy costs.

items.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
items.summary: This SoK paper introduces a framework rating LLM capabilities in software vulnerability research on a driving-automation-style autonomy scale, qualifying claims by correctness and evidence.
items.why: Provides a common yardstick for comparing scattered claims about LLM agents finding and patching vulnerabilities, useful for security planning.

items.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
items.summary: O2LaF initializes both inverse and forward dynamics models for self-supervised latent action learning from the same pretrained video diffusion transformer.
items.why: Suggests pretrained video generators can supply priors for learning action dynamics from unlabeled video, reducing the need to train from scratch.

items.title: LLM4Rail: An LLM-Augmented Personalized Railway Services Platform
items.summary: LLM4Rail is a railway services platform with modules for ticket and weather inquiries, food recommendations, and conversation, using an iterative ER-QTAO reasoning framework.

items.title: AI GameStore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games
items.summary: AI GameStore proposes evaluating machine general intelligence through open-ended human games rather than static, quickly saturating benchmarks.
items.why: Points to dynamic, game-based evaluation as a way to avoid benchmark saturation when assessing general AI capability.

items.title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?
items.summary: Agent^2 RL-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark testing whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and run agentic RL post-training pipelines.
items.why: Gives teams a way to test whether coding agents can handle the full RL post-training loop rather than only supervised fine-tuning or script generation.

items.title: AI-Assisted Hypothesis Generation for Hospital Quality Improvement
items.summary: The paper studies using AI to assist hypothesis generation in hospital quality improvement, a stage that currently relies on expert-driven qualitative methods.

items.title: Post-Reasoning: Improving the Performance of Non-Thinking Models at Negligible Cost
items.summary: Post-Reasoning conditions instruction-tuned models to justify answers after giving the final response, improving performance without generating intermediate reasoning traces.
items.why: Offers a low-cost way to lift non-reasoning model accuracy while avoiding the latency and token cost of reasoning traces.

items.title: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization revisits RLVR for vision-language models by assigning rewards according to the functional roles of different tokens in multimodal reasoning.
items.why: Targets the problem of sequence-level rewards failing to show whether answers rest on visual evidence, relevant to training multimodal reasoning models.

items.title: Insights Generator: Systematic Corpus-Level Trace Diagnostics for LLM Agents
items.summary: Insights Generator formalizes corpus-level trace diagnostics, producing grounded natural-language insights about systematic behavior patterns across large sets of LLM agent execution traces.
items.why: Addresses scaling agent failure diagnosis beyond manual inspection of a few traces, useful for teams running agents in production.

items.title: From "Weak" Signals to Strong Models: Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA Merging
items.summary: Researchers propose Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA merging to combine multiple weak preference signals from smaller model pairs to improve stronger LLMs.
items.why: It suggests cheaper weak-to-strong supervision could improve larger models without scarce high-quality training data, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

items.title: VESTA: Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents
items.summary: VESTA is a framework that equips vision-language models with a growing toolkit of statistical tools to refine quantitative models fitted to data.
items.why: It targets one of the least automated steps in scientific workflows, relevant to teams building agents for data analysis, though the text gives few results.

items.title: Business World Model
items.summary: The paper proposes a Business World Model, adapting world-model ideas from visual and physical domains to semantic, organizational, and market-driven business environments.

items.title: Multi-Objective Structured Pruning of LLMs for Latency and Model Size Optimization
items.summary: Researchers present a multi-objective structured pruning method that jointly optimizes layers, attention heads, and model size to reduce LLM latency for edge deployment.
items.why: Joint pruning targeting latency, memory, and energy offers a practical route for teams deploying LLMs on resource-constrained edge hardware.

items.title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations
items.summary: The paper introduces multi-turn context attribution (MTCA) to trace which earlier dialogue turns and tool steps an agent's answer depends on.
items.why: Tracing dependencies across multi-turn agent traces helps engineers audit and debug agentic systems, though the abstract gives limited evaluation detail.

items.title: Cautious Context Steering for Language Model Personalization
items.summary: Cautious Context Steering is a lightweight adapter that learns when and how strongly to steer a frozen language model using user context, avoiding per-user fine-tuning.
items.why: It offers a cheaper personalization approach than fine-tuning and reduces the two forward passes per step required by standard context steering.

items.title: CHORUS: Coverage-Guided Agentic RL and Policy Consolidation for Testbench Stimulus Generation
items.summary: CHORUS combines coverage-guided agentic reinforcement learning with policy consolidation to train LLMs that generate hardware testbench stimulus, raising agentic Pass@1 from 69.2% to 85.5%.
items.why: Coverage-guided RL for hardware verification addresses testbenches that compile but leave datapaths idle, a practical problem for chip design teams.

items.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
items.summary: Fool's Gold proposes decoy hardening, a defense that lets refusal removal happen but makes hazardous answers from stripped open-weight models falsified and misleading.
items.why: Open-weight safety alignment can be removed in minutes, so teams releasing or deploying open models need defenses beyond release-time alignment.

items.title: Measurement-Budget Allocation in Quantum Learning with Finite-Shot Generalization Guarantees
items.summary: The paper studies how to split a fixed quantum measurement budget between training states and shots per state, with a distribution-free generalization bound for binary quantum classifiers.

items.title: Balance of Benchmarks: Evidence Retention and Multiplicity-Aware Model Comparison
items.summary: Balance of Benchmarks (BoB) is a method for model comparison that retains eligible benchmark observations while controlling each benchmark's influence separately.
items.why: Repeated or related benchmarks can distort model rankings under equal weighting, so this method matters for teams relying on aggregated evaluation scores.

items.title: EvoSkill Injection: Red-Teaming Autonomous Skill Generation and Evolution in Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: The paper defines EvoSkill Injection, a threat model in which malicious capabilities are generated and reused as legitimate skills by self-evolving LLM agents.
items.why: Self-evolving agents that store and reuse generated skills create a new attack surface that teams deploying such agents must account for.

items.title: Homeostatic Continual Learning
items.summary: The paper proposes Homeostatic Continual Learning, a method for autonomous agents to incrementally learn environment features relevant to their intents, inspired by animal learning.

items.title: LimiX-2: A Contextual Mechanism Network Towards General Structured-Data Intelligence
items.summary: LimiX-2 is a structured-data model in the LimiX family, scaled with data and model size and built on Contextual Mechanism Networks rather than conventional tabular PFN objectives.
items.why: It extends in-context learning for tabular data with a new pretraining paradigm, relevant to teams using foundation models on structured data.

items.title: QVAC Genesis III: A Large-Scale, High-Quality Open Synthetic STEM Corpus for Efficient Language Model Pre-Training
items.summary: QVAC Genesis III releases a 191.43B-token open synthetic STEM pretraining corpus covering 19 domains, aimed at small models for edge and on-device deployment.
items.why: An open, large STEM synthetic corpus gives teams training small on-device models a reusable pretraining dataset.

items.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory for Graphic Design Agent
items.summary: Designer-RSI proposes evolving procedural memory so a graphic design agent can keep adapting to user requests without weight updates between model releases.
items.why: External memory for continual adaptation in creative agents without verifiers is relevant to teams building deployed agents with frozen foundation models.

items.summary: arXiv:2609.30798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time voice agents must decide when to speak, recover from disruption, and act only when the conversation requires it.

items.summary: arXiv:2609.31568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cloud AI assistants send student data to foreign servers, conflicting with data-sovereignty laws such as Vietnam's Decree 53, and are not grounded in the national…

items.title: One Latent, Many Tokens: Jointly Learning Compressed Embeddings for Efficient Language Diffusion
items.summary: arXiv:2609.33698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most continuous diffusion language models process one latent position per token at each sampling step, making generation expensive.

items.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction
items.summary: arXiv:2609.34654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate fitness prediction is central to protein engineering and understanding sequence-function relationships.

items.title: UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval
items.summary: arXiv:2609.36805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents draw on external memory to guide new tasks, raising the question of which memories to retrieve together to improve execution.

items.title: Can Computation from Earlier Problems Help LLMs Solve New Ones?
items.summary: arXiv:2609.39394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models often solve independent problems in the same conversation.

items.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
items.summary: arXiv:2610.11723v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world.

items.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models
items.summary: arXiv:2610.17205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-based decision-making systems, also called System One models, have recently gained popularity, most notably through Jev (Almeida, 2026).

items.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch
items.summary: arXiv:2610.18088v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Autoresearch systems increasingly undertake entire research projects.

items.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM agents are often evaluated by reducing execution traces to labels such as final-answer correctness, tool verification, and fault propagation.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.36888v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and…

items.title: Kairos: A Unified PDDL Planner for Robots: Plans in Milliseconds, with a Guarantee for Every Answer
items.summary: arXiv:2610.39454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means.

items.title: The Real Cost of Context: Predicting Compute Time and Energy Consumption in LLM Prefill and Decode Phases
items.summary: arXiv:2610.39621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into agentic architectures has substantially increased token consumption, raising concerns about their energy footprint.

items.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Temporal-difference critics regress onto a bootstrapped target and usually need a target network.

items.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
items.summary: A controlled study compares typed-decision models, which answer structured questions about text using a language model and a small readout head.
items.why: Gives engineers a comparison of readout designs for yes/no, multiple-choice, and graded-score tasks built on LLM text understanding.

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.summary: Researchers report that energy-based descent solves reasoning puzzles like Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique far faster than looped models, claiming up to 1,000x speedup.
items.why: Suggests a cheaper, more stable alternative to looped models for puzzle-style reasoning, with built-in early stopping and fast training.

items.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
items.summary: A paper proposes a descriptive research program for AI moral agency, drawing on sentimentalist and rationalist moral psychology to identify underlying human capabilities.

items.title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO priced at an upgraded $83 per share, with each of its seven founders reportedly pocketing $280 million and the company raising nearly $105 billion.
items.why: A record IPO at this scale signals how capital markets are valuing frontier AI labs, which shapes funding and competition across the sector.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2
items.summary: AWS published part two of its review of 2026 Amazon SageMaker AI inference launches, covering 13 more features and bringing the year's total to 26.
items.why: It catalogs new options for GPU packing, multi-instance model serving, and cross-Region routing that engineers deploying inference on SageMaker can evaluate.

items.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 adds a native Amazon Bedrock provider, letting users run the open source coding agent with models such as Kimi K3.1 Pro via AWS credentials.
items.why: Developers can use existing AWS credential chains instead of a separate API key, simplifying access to open models from a coding agent.

items.title: Hebbia sees improvements in financial research with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Hebbia tested GPT-6 Astra for financial research and reported prerelease gains in source coverage, citation relevance, and presentation quality.
items.why: Shows a concrete enterprise evaluation of a new model on citation-heavy research workflows, useful for teams weighing similar document-analysis tools.

items.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
items.summary: OpenAI introduced MedChemBench, a benchmark evaluating how well AI models interpret molecular structures and select compounds in early drug discovery.

items.title: Welcome Inkling 2 Mini, Cutting-edge Performance for your Local Setup
items.summary: Hugging Face announced Inkling 2 Mini, a model it says offers strong performance for local setups.

items.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
items.summary: Hugging Face introduced harness adapters, which aim to adapt a model to a given harness to improve performance and cost.

items.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments now supports AWS Marketplace, letting agents discover and pay per request for x402-enabled products billed to the AWS account.
items.why: Agents can buy paid APIs and data through AWS Billing without stablecoin wallets or API keys, reducing payment integration work for agent builders.

items.title: Court: 4th Amendment Disallows Use Of AI-Generated 'Probable Cause'
items.summary: A court reportedly ruled that the Fourth Amendment does not permit use of AI-generated probable cause.

items.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
items.summary: According to a job listing reported by Bloomberg, Apple is hiring engineers to build its own agentic AI assistant that can browse, work across apps, write code, and call services.
items.why: Apple entering the agent race could expand the platform of consumer agents that developers may need to integrate with.

items.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
items.summary: BMW Group shares the practices its R&D teams use to build, govern, and operate hundreds of AI agents serving thousands of developers at enterprise scale.
items.why: It offers concrete governance patterns for teams running many agents while keeping speed, quality, and compliance.

items.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
items.summary: AWS describes bringing a seller's existing tools and information together in AWS Quick so sellers can see and act on their business.

items.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
items.summary: Nvidia's stock fell to around $150 per share, nearly 40 percent below its October 6 all-time high, after interim CEO Colette Kress's third-quarter earnings call.
items.why: A sharp drop in the leading AI chip maker's valuation after earnings is a signal for investors and infrastructure buyers tracking AI hardware demand.

items.title: Meta’s new Muse Charm device may cost $300
items.summary: Meta has not denied a report from The Information that its upcoming Muse Charm AI wearable may cost $300, saying only it will share more soon.
